title: Théorie arithmétique. Théorie de Galois des motifs (1965) : notes manuscites (s.d.), tapuscrit (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is not Grothendieck's own mathematics. It is a typescript page (numbered '- 26 -') from a Bourbaki-style draft on analytic differential equations over a complete valued field K. It cites '§1, th.2 (théorème de substitution)', '§1, prop.8' and 'Fonct. var. réelle, chap. IV'. Its verso was reused as scrap paper for the handwritten notes on Deuring/Brandt categories (previous and next pages); the bleed-through matches.

Content, in modern terms:
(1) The page ends the proof of an analytic existence theorem (Cauchy–Kovalevskaya type for ODEs with parameters) by the method of majorants.
- The system is majorized by the scalar ODE (19): dv/dt = M / ((1−αt)(1−pαv)(1−αΣ_{ℓ=1}^q v_ℓ)).
- The parameters v_ℓ are treated as constants. Separating variables, the solution vanishing at t=0 satisfies v − (pα/2)v² = −M log(1−αt) / (α(1−αΣv_ℓ)).
- Solving the quadratic gives a closed form for v(t).
- Since log(1−αt) is a convergent power series without constant term for |t|<1/α, the substitution theorem shows v is a power series in t, v_1, …, v_q. It has no term independent of t and converges in a polycylinder at the origin.
- The majorized series therefore converge, which proves the theorem: an analytic solution exists for analytic f_i with analytic parameters z_1, …, z_q.

(2) Remark for K = R: analytic f_i are locally Lipschitz in the y_j, so the classical uniqueness theorem applies. The unique C¹ solution is therefore real-analytic.

(3) Start of §4, 'Applications I: dependence on initial conditions'. Proposition 1 sets up:
- K a complete valued field of characteristic 0;
- f_i(x; y_1..y_p) holomorphic on A = B×C ⊂ K^{p+1};
- for (a,b) ∈ A there are neighbourhoods U of a and V of b, and u(x, x_0, y_0) holomorphic on U×U×V with values in C;
- for each (x_0, y_0), x ↦ u(x, x_0, y_0) is the unique holomorphic solution near x_0 of the ODE (continuation on the next typescript page).
This is the standard analytic flow / holomorphic dependence on initial data, valid over any complete valued field including p-adic fields. It is the material behind analytic (Lie) groups over such fields, as in Bourbaki's Variétés différentielles et analytiques and Serre's Lie Algebras and Lie Groups, Part II.
errors: The displayed closed form is wrong as typed. Solving v − (pα/2)v² = c with c = −M log(1−αt)/(α(1−αΣv_ℓ)) gives v = (1/(pα))[1 − √(1 − 2pM log(1−αt)/(1−αΣv_ℓ))].

The typescript has the prefactor pα instead of 1/(pα), and '+' instead of '−' inside the square root. These are typing slips; they do not affect the argument, which only needs analyticity of the expression near t=0.
Minor point: the argument implicitly treats the v_ℓ as constants when integrating (19). This is legitimate since no derivative in the v_ℓ is involved, but it is not stated.

ideas.what: Method of majorants proving convergence of formal solutions of analytic ODEs with parameters over a complete valued field, via an explicitly integrable scalar comparison equation
ideas.modern_name: Cauchy majorant method / Cauchy–Kovalevskaya for ODEs over complete valued fields
ideas.usually_credited_to: Cauchy; the general valued-field setting appears in Bourbaki and Serre (1960s)
ideas.where_published: Bourbaki, Variétés différentielles et analytiques (fascicule de résultats); Serre, Lie Algebras and Lie Groups (1965), Part II

ideas.what: Holomorphic dependence of solutions on initial conditions (analytic flow u(x, x_0, y_0)) over a complete valued field of characteristic 0
ideas.modern_name: Analytic dependence on initial data / local analytic flow
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Cauchy, Poincaré); p-adic version in Bourbaki/Serre
ideas.where_published: Bourbaki VDA; Serre LALG Part II

ideas.what: For K=R, Lipschitz uniqueness combined with analytic existence gives analyticity of the unique solution
ideas.where_published: Bourbaki, Fonctions d'une variable réelle, ch. IV

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a reused Bourbaki-style typescript on standard analytic ODE theory over valued fields. It has no connection to Grothendieck's motivic or Deuring-category notes on the other side, and its content is classical apart from a typo in the closed-form solution.
transcription_corrections: Closed form as typed reads v(t) = pα[1 − √(1 + (2pM/(1−αΣv_ℓ)) log(1−αt))]; the transcription matches the image, but the formula itself is mathematically wrong (should be (1/(pα))[1 − √(1 − …)]).
In Proposition 1 the function u takes values 'dans C' (the open set C ⊂ K^p), not 'dans U' as the bleed-through note on the previous page has it.
The page number is likely '- 26 -' (partly faded).
